name: Magnetite
equilibrium_context: Verwey transition (insulator-metal, charge and orbital order, trimeron network) at 123 K

driven_states.emergent_property: The transition proceeds in two stages: first the destruction of individual trimerons (300 fs), then phase separation (1.5 ps) into remaining insulating and metallic regions. The 1.5 ps set the speed limit of the Verwey transition.
driven_states.source: de Jong et al., Nature Materials 12, 882 (2013), doi:10.1038/nmat3718
further_sources: PNAS 121, e2316438121 (2024), doi:10.1073/pnas.2316438121 (two distinct metastable structural hidden phases depending on photon energy)
driven_states.caveat: The work deliberately speaks of a speed limit precisely because the transition is not purely electronic: the 1.5 ps are a phase-separation and nucleation time, hence first order with lattice involvement. The initial electronic stage of 300 fs, by contrast, is well established as non-thermal. The 2024 PNAS work is the strongest non-thermal argument, because the resulting state depends on the photon energy - pure heating cannot do that.
